ai_show_review.summary: Scarlet>Fire blaze, soaring Morning Dew and tight rhythm fuel a high‑energy show
ai_show_review.blurb: The band delivers a blistering Scarlet Begonias → Fire on the Mountain segue, followed by an inspired second‑set flow through Estimated Prophet, Eyes Of The World and a birthday‑shout Morning Dew. Jerry’s guitar shines, Brent’s keyboards add fuel, and the dual drummers lock in with extra‑arm intensity.
ai_show_review.review: Manor Downs on July 31 1982 finds the Dead firing on all cylinders. The first set rolls from an upbeat Alabama Getaway into a crisp Candyman where Garcia’s vocals sparkle and Brent layers bright harmonies, while Bird Song already hints at the night’s elevated vibe. The real highlight erupts in the second set: a smoking Scarlet Begonias → Fire on the Mountain transition that feels both seamless and explosive, then a soaring Estimated Prophet that flows into Eyes Of The World with crystal‑clear matrix‑like separation. Space opens the door for the twin‑drummer conversation; Mickey and Bill weave an intricate tapestry before launching Uncle John’s Band straight into Truckin’ without missing a beat. The climax arrives with a birthday‑shout Morning Dew—Garcia’s voice raw, his lead soaring over Brent’s lush keys—and a rousing One More Saturday Night to close the set, followed by a gentle Don’t Ease Me In encore. Across all sources the rhythm section is tight and powerful, Phil’s bass thunders like a “bass beast,” and Bob’s rhythm work anchors each jam. Whether you listen to the Miller soundboard or the pristine matrix, this performance stands out as one of the band’s high‑energy summer highlights.

best_recording.reason: Solid soundboard mix with crisp, balanced audio; captures the high‑energy performance and key moments (Candyman, Scarlet>Fire, Morning Dew) with minimal technical issues.

key_highlights: Smoking Scarlet Begonias → Fire on the Mountain segue that drives the second set
Soaring Morning Dew featuring Jerry’s birthday shout and pristine vocal delivery
Tight dual‑drummer interplay described as ‘eight arms’ delivering powerful percussion
Brent Mydland’s vibrant keyboards adding fuel to jams like Estimated Prophet and Eyes Of The World

band_performance.Jerry: Top‑form guitar tone and strong vocals, especially on Candyman and the birthday‑shout Morning Dew; leads the band with inspiring solos throughout.
band_performance.Phil: Bass is a ‘beast firing bombs,’ providing a solid foundation for extended jams; occasional thinness noted but overall powerful.
band_performance.Bob: Steady rhythm guitar and vocal work, highlighted on Bird Song and the second‑set flow; locks in tightly with the band.
band_performance.Brent: Keyboard work is clear, vibrant and adds fuel to the improvisations; provides vocal harmonies on Candyman and drives the texture of Estimated Prophet and Eyes Of The World.
band_performance.Mickey: Drums lock with Bill for an extra‑step performance, delivering tight, powerful percussion that propels the set.
band_performance.Billy: Shares the percussive onslaught, contributing to the ‘eight‑arm’ feel; maintains a solid groove throughout.
